short: Japan's AI Promotion Act has been fully in force since 1 September 2025 and contains no penalties; the binding layer is the privacy law, the APPI, whose 2026 amendment adds surcharges.
title: Japan AI Laws
subtitle: The AI Promotion Act, a statute with no penalties by design
body_html:
Status at a glance

AI law in force, without penalties. Japan's AI Promotion Act (人工知能関連技術の研究開発及び活用の推進に関する法律, Act No. 53 of 2025) passed the Diet on 28 May 2025, was promulgated on 4 June 2025 and has been fully in force since 1 September 2025. It is a real statute with no fines, no bans and no penalty chapter: it organises government action through the AI Strategic Headquarters and the AI Basic Plan, and asks businesses to cooperate. The enforceable layer is the privacy law, the Act on the Protection of Personal Information (APPI), which was amended in 2026 to add surcharges. Verified on 25 October 2026 against e-Gov, the House of Councillors, the Cabinet Office and the Personal Information Protection Commission.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberPassedPromulgatedIn force
AI Promotion ActAct No. 53 of 202528 May 2025 (House of Councillors; House of Representatives 24 April 2025)4 June 2025In part 4 June 2025; in full 1 September 2025
AI Basic Plan (Art. 18)Cabinet decision23 December 2025; second plan 14 July 2026Policy, not law
Amendment to the Act on the Protection of Personal InformationAct No. 56 of 202610 July 202617 July 2026Not yet in force; in principle within two years of promulgation

Who regulates and enforces

  • AI Strategic Headquarters, in the Cabinet (Art. 19), with the Cabinet Office as secretariat; it issues guidance under Article 13.
  • Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC): enforces the APPI, including the new surcharge orders once they apply.

Scope and reach

The Act addresses the State, local governments, research and development bodies, businesses that use AI (活用事業者, Art. 7) and citizens. It has no extraterritorial trigger and nothing to enforce against a business; Article 7 asks businesses to cooperate with State measures, without sanction.

Core obligations

  • Businesses using AI shall cooperate with national and local measures (Art. 7), with no sanction attached.
  • The State issues guidelines in line with international norms (Art. 13), researches rights infringements from improper AI use, and gives guidance, advice and information (Art. 16).
  • The government adopts the AI Basic Plan (Art. 18).
  • The binding layer is the APPI, which governs the personal data AI systems process.

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Anything under the AI Promotion ActNone: the Act has no penalty provisionsAct, Chapters 1 to 4 and supplementary provisions
APPI database offences or breach of PPC orders, by a corporationA fine of up to JPY 100 millionAPPI Art. 184(1)(i)Courts, on the PPC's referral
APPI infringements once Act No. 56 of 2026 appliesA surcharge equal to the illicit gain, in cases measured against 1,000 or more affected peopleNew APPI Arts. 148-3 to 148-17PPC

What is coming next

  • 17 January 2027: first provisions of the APPI amendment take effect, according to e-Gov's revision record.
  • By 16 July 2028: the APPI amendment's main provisions, including surcharges, take effect.
